topic.title: Logarithmic Functions
topic.summary: The domain, range, vertical asymptote, and end behavior of logarithmic functions, why they have no extrema or points of inflection, and recognizing a logarithmic pattern after an additive transformation.

variants.stem: Let f(x) = a log_b x, where a = −2 and b = 1/3.

parts.prompt: Find the domain of f.
Find the range of f.
Find lim x→0⁺ f(x).

solution: The domain of a logarithmic function in general form is all x > 0, because only positive numbers can be written as a power of the base.
The range of a logarithmic function in general form is all real numbers.
The graph of f has the vertical asymptote x = 0. With a < 0 and 0 < b < 1, f is increasing, so f(x) approaches −∞ as x approaches 0 from the right.

variants.stem: The graph of the logarithmic function f(x) = a log₃ x is shown. Points on the graph are marked.

stimulusBlocks.caption: The graph of y = f(x)
stimulusBlocks.alt: A decreasing logarithmic curve that has the y-axis as a vertical asymptote and passes through (1, 0), (3, −1), (9, −2).

parts.prompt: Find lim x→0⁺ f(x).
Find lim x→∞ f(x).
Is f increasing or decreasing on its domain?
Find the x-intercept of the graph of f.

solution: As x approaches 0 from the right, the graph rises without bound along the asymptote x = 0, so lim x→0⁺ f(x) = ∞.
As x increases without bound the graph falls without bound, so lim x→∞ f(x) = −∞.
The marked points show the outputs decreasing as x increases, so f is decreasing.
Every logarithmic function in general form has f(1) = 0, because b⁰ = 1. The x-intercept is at x = 1.

parts.prompt: Is f increasing or decreasing on its domain?
Is the graph of f concave up or concave down on its domain?
Find the x-value at which f has its absolute maximum on the closed interval [4, 9].

solution: With a > 0 and b > 1, a logarithmic function is always increasing.
With a > 0 and b > 1, the graph is always concave down.
Because f is always increasing, the largest output on [4, 9] occurs at the right endpoint, x = 9.

variants.stem: The table gives values of a function g. The function g can be written as g(x) = f(x + k), where f is a logarithmic function and k is a constant.

parts.prompt: What number k, added to each input, makes the new inputs proportional?
What is the constant ratio between consecutive values of x + k?
Write an expression for g(x).

solution: The outputs increase by 1 each time, but the inputs 0, 2, 8, 26 are not proportional. Adding 1 gives 1, 3, 9, 27, which are proportional. So k = 1.
Each new input is 3 times the one before it, so the ratio is 3.
The shifted inputs x + 1 are powers of 3 and the outputs are the exponents, so g(x) = log₃(x + 1).
